**Narrative — Eicosanoid Dysregulation in the Treatment Group**

The RaMP enrichment analysis identifies **Eicosanoid Synthesis (WikiPathways WP167)** as the top candidate pathway (FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment ≈ 1001), with five of the ten input metabolites — arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 5-HETE (C04805), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) — mapping to it. A secondary high-confidence hit is **Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency (SMP00353)**, which shares the same five matched compounds.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the central hub: KEGG membership queries confirm it is annotated in the Arachidonic Acid Metabolism pathway (map00590), and the graph traversal confirms it is the obligate precursor. From it, the 5-lipoxygenase branch leads to leukotriene A4 (C00909), and the 12/15-lipoxygenase branch leads to 15-HETE (C04742). Both branches are active downstream of the hub (paths of length 2 confirmed via `query_kegg_path`). The cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) is also annotated in the Arachidonic Acid Metabolism pathway (map00590), consistent with shared substrate origins.

**Biological significance.** Coordinated elevation of arachidonate-derived lipid mediators points to treatment-induced activation of phospholipase A2, releasing membrane arachidonic acid, followed by parallel stimulation of 5-LOX, 12/15-LOX, and COX-2 branches. Leukotriene A4 is a potent chemoattractant for neutrophils; 15-HETE and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 are immunomodulatory eicosanoids with roles in resolving inflammation. The concurrent presence of 5-HETE (also a 5-LOX product) strengthens the case for widespread eicosanoid pathway activation. Copper (C00070), which appears in the Selenium Micronutrient Network (WP15), may act as a cofactor for antioxidant enzymes that normally dampen eicosanoid-driven inflammation. Histamine (C00388) and gentisic acid (C00628) suggest ancillary oxidative-stress and phenolic-antioxidant responses. Dihydrothymine (C00906), while not part of the eicosanoid core, is consistent with downstream nucleobase stress [disputed by verifier].

**Verified upstream/downstream relationships:** Arachidonic acid (C00219) → Leukotriene A4 (C00909) via 5-HPETE (C05356); Arachidonic acid (C00219) → 15-HETE (C04742) via 15-HPETE (C05966) — both paths confirmed.

**Limitations.** Hypochlorite (C19697) and copper (C00070) did not map to the top-ranked Eicosanoid Synthesis pathway; their enrichment in the broader Selenium Micronutrient Network is plausible but not mechanistically linked to arachidonate metabolism via the KEGG graph, and the precise upstream trigger for the concurrent oxidative-stress signature remains inferential.
